question.text: Fund CAS, a Category III AIF pursuing Convertible Arbitrage, takes a long position in Company A's 12% convertible bond and a simultaneous short position in Company A's equity shares. If Company A's equity price RISES significantly above the conversion price, the fund will typically:

answer.text: Hold the bond to maturity and let the short position compound losses indefinitely
Convert the convertible security into equity shares and sell those shares at market value, compensating for the loss on the short position
Close both legs at a loss because the arbitrage has broken down permanently
Roll the bond forward and double the short position to restore the hedge

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.2.3 (Convertible Arbitrage Strategy), if equity price rises the fund can convert the convertible security into equity shares and sell the equity shares at market value to compensate for the short-position losses. Example 11.6 illustrates this mechanism. The Trap: Option A ignores the conversion option that is the whole point of the strategy. Option C misreads a successful outcome as failure. Option D adds risk rather than using the embedded conversion option. Note: The conversion-and-sell mechanic is what offsets the mark-to-market loss on the short leg when equity rises.
